text:
ashwin: heads-up — I pushed a new observability panel for prompt-cache token-saved breakdown (by model / route / customer). Noticed a ~22% drop in token-saved for redwood-13b-ql on /chat/send for AcmeCorp starting ~4h ago.

olga: link? can you paste the grafana panel id so I can jump in?

ashwin: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/7qXkS/prompt-cache-hitstory?panelId=9 — main query is the per-route token_saved metric grouped by model and customer.

kevin: deploy-bot shows a runtime kernel selector rollout at 3220 (canary) ~5h ago — possible correlation. deploy-bot: canary rollout to kernel-v2 with batching heuristics change "adaptive_window=0.8" completed for 10% of capacity. :robot_face:

jordan: interesting — kernel selection could affect KV cache keying if sequence length assumptions changed. did the rollout include any kv-cache key normalization changes?

ashwin: not that I saw in the runtime diff. The change was mostly kernel/kernel-sched heuristics + batch window tuning. No intentional key normalization.

maria: I ran a quick prefix-key cardinality query over the same window — saw ~1.6x increase in unique keys for AcmeCorp /chat/send for redwood-13b-ql starting with the rollout timeframe. Query: ``SELECT count(distinct(prefix_hash)) FROM prompt_cache WHERE route='/chat/send' AND customer='AcmeCorp' AND model='redwood-13b-ql' AND ts > now() - 6h``

kevin: if unique keys jumped, hit-rate would drop even with same request volume. Could be a subtle change in batch-padding or tokenization that makes exact-match keys differ. Any changes to tokenizer config?

ashwin: no tokenizer changes on model side. But kernel-v2 switched to trimming trailing whitespace from the prefix before computing the cache fingerprint (looks like a micro-optimization for KV memory locality). That could explain it.

jordan: aha — trimming sounds harmless but if clients occasionally send trailing spaces (we've seen that per-route), keys shift. We should check prefix-keying logic and add normalization at hashing layer instead of runtime kernel change.

sam: quick repro idea: take a sample of incoming prefixes (pre-rollout vs post-rollout) and diff their normalized vs raw hashes. I can script that and dump counts. Want me to run it?

ashwin: please do. Also add a temporal slice for other models, e.g., redwood-3b and redwood-7b-q to see extent.

perf-bot: perf-alert: prompt-cache hit-rate drop detected for model=redwood-13b-ql route=/chat/send customer=AcmeCorp threshold=15% severity=medium

olga: ops playbook: can we revert kernel-v2 trimming quickly if this proves to be the cause? Is that change gated behind a feature flag?

kevin: it's behind runtime flag `kv_hash_trim_ws=true` — currently only on 10% canary. We can flip it off on those hosts while we patch.

maria: I ran sam's diff locally (v1 vs v2 prefixes). Results: ~21% of post-rollout prefixes had differing normalized-hash due to trailing ws removal. Sample snippet: ``prefix_raw='Order status ' -> raw_hash=0x8a3f... normalized_strip='Order status' -> hash=0x5c1b...``

jordan: that matches the 22% token-saved drop ashwin saw. Action items: (1) flip `kv_hash_trim_ws` off on canary hosts, (2) implement normalized keying in prompt_cache service (explicit canonicalization before hash), (3) add regression test to prevent kernel changes from mutating external keying semantics.

ashwin: +1. Also we should add a dashboard panel for "key-delta ratio" (fraction of prefixes whose normalized-hash != raw-hash) by model/route/customer so future kernel experiments surface this quickly.

kevin: I'll flip the flag now and watch. If hit-rate recovers in next 15-30m we can tie the regression to this.

deploy-bot: toggle: kv_hash_trim_ws=false applied to hosts in canary pool at 3287654375

ashwin: watching the token-saved panel — bumping already.

perf-bot: perf-update: token-saved for redwood-13b-ql /chat/send / AcmeCorp increased from -22% delta -> -2% within 12m of toggle.

olga: good rollback signal. Next: plan for canonicalization PR and tests. Who owns?

maria: I'll open the PR for prompt-cache canonicalization and include a unit test that simulates kernel-level whitespace trimming. I'll also add the new dashboard panel in the observability repo.

jordan: I'll add a note to the kernel rollout checklist that any change touching prefix bytes must be paired with a keying-compat review.

ashwin: thanks everyone. Great fast diagnosis. I'll create a follow-up thread for the PR review/QA once maria opens it. :thumbsup:
